title: ように: one key to all the main uses
summary: よう means "form, state". Clause + ようになる is entering that state, ようにする is bringing it about, and a wish ends with ように.

blocks.text: Start with a reminder. **なる** (become) is the moving partner of **ある** (be). **する** (do, make) is the other-move partner. With a noun: 蛙**になる** (turn into a frog), 蛙**にする** (turn something into a frog).
よう is a noun: a state
**よう** means "form, manner, state". Put a whole clause in front of it and the clause describes that state: 日本語が話せる**よう**, "the state of Japanese being speakable". Then it is a normal noun + に.
ようになる: entering the state
This is a **change of state**: you came to be in the state the clause describes.

blocks.jp: 日本語が話せるようになった。
blocks.en: I have become able to speak Japanese.

blocks.jp: 彼を信じるようになった。

blocks.text: ようにする: bringing it about
The other-move partner: you make the state happen, or **try to make sure** it does. Said of yourself, it means "I make a point of ..." without promising success.

blocks.jp: 毎日運動するようにしている。
blocks.en: I make a point of exercising every day.

blocks.jp: 忘れ物をしないようにしてください。
blocks.en: Please make sure you do not forget anything.

blocks.text: Purpose: the same thing with a real verb
The "in order that" use is not a new pattern. する is the neutral all-purpose action; swap it for a specific action and you get a purpose: "do X so that the state comes about".

blocks.jp: 風邪をひかないように、厚い服を着た。
blocks.en: I wore thick clothes so as not to catch a cold.

blocks.text: A sentence can end with ように as a prayer or wish, a shortened ようにしてください addressed to a god or the stars.

blocks.jp: 日本に行けますように。
blocks.en: May I be able to go to Japan!

items: **Clause + ようになる**: change into that state (came to ...).
**Clause + ようにする**: make it so / try to make sure.
**Clause + ように** at the end: a wish.

questions.prompt: 毎日練習したら、泳げるようになった。
options: I decided to swim every day
questions.note: ようになる: you came to be in the state of being able.
questions.en: After practicing every day, I became able to swim.

questions.prompt: 毎晩、早く寝る＿＿している。
questions.note: ようにする: make a point of doing it.
questions.en: I make a point of going to bed early every night.

questions.prompt: 子供が起きない＿＿、静かに歩いた。
questions.note: Purpose: clause + ように, then the action.
questions.en: I walked quietly so the child would not wake up.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I have come to eat vegetables" (a change of state)?
options: 野菜を食べますように。
野菜を食べるようにしてください。
野菜を食べるようになった。
questions.note: ようになった: entered the state of eating vegetables.

questions.prompt: ようにする guarantees that the thing really happens.
questions.note: It only says you try to bring it about.
questions.en: The pattern ようにする does not guarantee the result.

questions.instruction: What does よう mean on its own?
questions.note: よう is a noun: the state a clause describes.

questions.prompt: 彼は最近、朝ごはんを食べないようになった。
options: He makes a point of eating breakfast
He was told not to eat breakfast
He wishes he could eat breakfast
He has come to not eat breakfast
questions.note: Negative clause + ようになる: a change into the not-doing state.
questions.en: Lately he has stopped eating breakfast.

questions.prompt: ここに車を止めないようにしてください。
options: You have become unable to park here
Please make sure you do not park here
I wish I could park here
questions.note: ようにしてください: please make sure of it.
questions.en: Please make sure not to park a car here.

options: 早く元気になるようにする。
早く元気になりますように。
早く元気になるようになった。
早く元気になるようだ。
questions.note: A sentence ending in ように is a wish.

options: 毎日走るようになった。
毎日走るようにしている。
questions.note: It needs に: ようになった.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I left home early so as not to be late"?
options: 遅れるように、早く家を出た。
遅れないように、ゆっくり家を出た。
遅れないようだ、早く家を出た。
遅れないように、早く家を出た。
questions.note: Purpose: the action serves the state of not being late.

questions.instruction: What does ように mean here?
questions.prompt: 漢字が書けるように、毎日練習している。
questions.note: Action + ように, + verb: so that.
questions.en: I practice every day so that I can write kanji.

questions.instruction: How do ようになる and ようにする differ?
options: なる is a wish; する is a question
なる is a change of state; する is bringing it about
なる is past; する is future
questions.note: なる is the self-move partner, する the other-move one.

questions.prompt: I try not to eat too much.
questions.note: Clause + ようにしている.
questions.en: I try not to eat too much.

questions.prompt: I became able to ride a bicycle.
questions.note: Clause + ように + なった.
questions.en: I became able to ride a bicycle.

questions.prompt: Please make sure you lock the door.
questions.note: ようにしてください: make sure.
questions.en: Please make sure you lock the door.

questions.prompt: I became able to eat fish.
questions.note: Clause + ようになった.
questions.en: I became able to eat fish.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "I make a point of"
questions.note: ようにしている: trying to make it so.
questions.en: I make a point of reading the newspaper every morning.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that turns this into a wish
questions.note: A final ように is a wish.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "so that" (purpose)
questions.note: Clause + ように + action.
questions.en: I wrote a memo so as not to forget.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "came to"
questions.note: ようになった: entered the state.
questions.en: She has recently come to eat vegetables.

questions.prompt: In 〜ようになる, the clause in front of よう describes the state you enter.
questions.note: よう is the noun; the clause describes it.
questions.en: In ようになる, the clause before よう describes the state you enter.
